subject: Aleph Data — post-call tech action items: SDK, auth, routing & prompt governance
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@alephdata.com>, Marc Liu <marc.liu@alephdata.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-22T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Aleph Data — post-call tech action items: SDK, auth, routing & prompt governance

Hi Samira / Marc — great conversation earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from the technical side so we have a single playbook to share with your infra and security teams.

Summary of current ask (from today's discovery):
- Replace current search reranker with embeddings + reranker for internal docs (low latency, on-demand).
- Integrate LLM features into product via SDK: client-side calls for light features, server-side for sensitive ops.
- Support OAuth2 / SAML SSO for users and service-to-service JWT for backend calls.
- Structured output for tool-calling (invoice extraction, entity normalization) and guardrails for prompt injection.

Proposed immediate items we can deliver in PoC (weeks 1–3):
1) SDK quickstart: we will hand over an "Aleph Quickstart" repo (Node + Python) showing token handling, streaming, error handling, and local integration tests.
2) Auth: recommend service-to-service using JWT + short-lived keys (we can provide an example JWKS endpoint + key rotation policy). For user auth, Redwood supports OIDC/OAuth + SAML via your IdP — we can exchange metadata for SSO testing.
3) Routing & policies: router rules to send low-latency requests to smaller models and cost-tiered requests to quantized variants. We will provide JSON examples of policy rules.
4) Embeddings & rerank: sample pipeline using dense embeddings (OpenSearch / Pinecone style upsert sample) and a re-ranker prompt template that runs server-side.
5) Prompt governance: kickoff with a versioned prompt repo, automated tests (unit prompts), and a simple red-team checklist.

Attachments: Aleph-Quickstart-SDK.md (quickstart + sample code), aleph-poc-data-map.xlsx (sample fields we discussed).

Immediate asks for Aleph team (can you confirm):
- Which IdP do you use for SSO (Okta, Azure AD, other)?
- Do you have a preferred embeddings vector store for the PoC, or should we spin up a short-lived store?
- Are there specific PII/data residency constraints we should lock into the PoC?

Proposed next meeting: 30-minute technical onboarding with your infra + security folks next Tuesday (Aug 24) at 11:00 PT to exchange metadata and confirm SSO flow. I will bring Laura from our infra team for the runtime/ops details.

If that works, I will follow up with a calendar invite + pre-read (SOW draft + quickstart).

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@alephdata.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marc Liu <marc.liu@alephdata.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aleph Data — post-call tech action items: SDK, auth, routing & prompt governance

Thanks Priyom — that aligns with what we covered. A couple clarifications from our side before the onboarding call: 

- IdP: We are on Okta (enterprise). We need SAML-based SSO for the product and OIDC for backend service accounts if possible.
- Data residency: customer documents must remain in our US-only cloud tenant for the PoC.
- Vector store: our infra team prefers to evaluate our in-house vector DB first; if that's not feasible, we can provision a Pinecone eval.
- Reranker: latency is critical for search — our SLO is p95 < 350ms for the search pipeline. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a server-side reranker and route to faster model variants?

We can do Aug 24 at 11:00 PT — Marc (our infra lead) will join and will send over the Okta metadata and an IP allowlist for initial testing.

Samira
VP, Product
Aleph Data
samira.k@alephdata.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@alephdata.com>, Marc Liu <marc.liu@alephdata.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-23T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aleph Data — post-call tech action items: SDK, auth, routing & prompt governance

Hi Samira / Marc — Laura from Redwood infra here. Thanks for the details — a few technical notes ahead of Tuesday's call to make the conversation concrete.

1) SDK & deployment patterns
- Quickstart will include Node/Python examples for both client-side (browser) and server-side (backend) usage. For any calls that touch customer PII or need deterministic outputs (rerankers, invoice parsing), please run server-side via service JWT.
- Sample config: use token scoping for per-route permissions, short ttl tokens (5–15m) for user agents, and refresh via your IdP.

2) Auth & SSO
- We support SAML SSO for product login; please send SAML metadata and ACS URLs.
- For backend-to-backend, we'll configure OIDC client_credentials with a JWKS endpoint. We'll share an example JWKS config and rotation script (attached in the quickstart).

3) Routing & fallback policies (important for latency SLO)
- Suggest rule set: if request_type == "search_rerank" and p95_target < 350ms -> route to model-compact-v2; else route to model-standard-v1.
- Automatic fallback: if preferred node pool is saturated, route to quantized variant with best-effort latency and tag response with "x-redwood-fallback: true".

4) Structured outputs & tool-calling
- We'll provide JSON-schema-driven structured output templates. For invoice extraction, we recommend a two-pass approach: extract -> normalize with rule-based post-processors.

5) Embeddings & rerank architecture
- Upsert pipeline: transform doc chunks -> compute embeddings -> metadata tagging -> store in vector DB.
- Re-ranker runs server-side against a top-K candidate set; it should be stateless and small model to hit p95 SLOs. We'll include performance profiles.

6) Prompt governance & red-team testing
- Versioning: we recommend a git repo for prompts with semantic version tags (v0.1, v0.2) and CI that runs unit prompt tests against a fixed evaluation set.
- Prompt injection mitigations: prefix/suffix guards, input sanitization (strip unexpected control characters), and deterministic structured-output validators.
- Red-team: table-top first (attack catalog), automated negative tests in CI, and a week-long external red-team run for high-risk templates.

Pre-reads: I attached the quickstart doc to Priyom's email thread; I'll upload a short runbook and the example JWKS rotation script to the Drive link before the call.

Action items for Tuesday:
- Aleph: share Okta SAML metadata + test account and IP allowlist.
- Redwood: share quickstart repo link, JWKS example, and a draft routing policy JSON.

I'll block 30 minutes on the calendar for Aug 24 11:00 PT and share invites.

Regards,

--
Laura Bennett
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Aleph PoC — red-team + prompts checklist and owner assignment

Ben / Laura — follow-up internal note after Samira's confirmation. I captured what we should bring to the PoC and owners. Please reply with any changes.

Owners and immediate tasks:
- Laura (infra): share JWKS rotation script + routing policy JSON by EOD Mon. Also prepare sample model-compact-v2 perf numbers for p95 latency.
- Ben (security): draft a short prompt red-team attack catalog and CI negative tests (start with invoice extraction and reranker templates).
- Priyom (me): provision the Quickstart repo, add PoC credentials (short-lived), and prepare the sample Drive docs for Aleph.

Checklist for PoC kickoff:
- Exchange SAML metadata + test accounts.
- Confirm vector store (Aleph in-house vs temporary Pinecone).
- Baseline perf: measure top-K retrieval + re-ranker p95.
- Prompt governance: set up prompt repo, add 5 initial templates and CI tests.

Ben — for the red-team catalog, prioritize injection vectors that target: structured-output overrides, overly-broad entity prompts, and malicious tool-calling signatures. Aim to have the first draft by Thu EOD so we can include it in the Aug 24 call.

I'll send the calendar invite and attach the SOW draft afterwards.

Thanks,

--
Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
